_note: Phase I.6 art budget — the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the curated set of oversized images that get downscaled in place. `tools/optimize-art.py` reads this to shrink them (idempotently: only files whose long edge exceeds `maxEdge` are touched); `test_art_budget.js` reads it to GUARD that they stay within budget (a re-added HD asset fails CI). Only deliberately-chosen, safe-to-downscale art is listed — NOT sprite sheets / tile atlases (hardcoded pixel cells) or .moc3 rig data. `maxEdge` is the cap on the longer image dimension in px; aspect ratio is preserved.

targets.note: peri model texture — was a single 8192px / 23 MB atlas (the plan's headline mistake). Live2D Cubism samples by NORMALIZED UVs, so downscaling the texture uniformly only lowers resolution; the rig (.moc3) is untouched.
peri-v2 model — 19 textures at 4096px (~53 MB) for an avatar rendered at scale 0.12. 2048px is ample; normalized UVs make this safe.
Companion scene backdrop — a plain background image, not a UV texture.
Square 1254px / 2.5 MB portrait — well above what the VN (≤~850px) or roster (200×240) ever shows.
Doubles as the zombie world-gate banner — downscaling it lightens the world-select screen too.
